claim_clusters.cluster_claim: The Inception-v3 architecture achieves state-of-the-art performance for single-crop/single-frame evaluation on the ILSVRC 2012 classification challenge, reporting 21.2% Top-1 Error and 5.6% Top-5 Error.

supported_by_papers.evidence: 21.2% top-1 and 5.6% top-5 error for single frame evaluation using a network with a computational cost of 5 billion multiply-adds per inference and with using less than 25 million parameters.

Our highest quality version of Inception-v3 reaches 21.2%, top-1 and 5.6% top-5 error for single crop evaluation on the ILSVR 2012 classification, setting a new state of the art.

claim_clusters.cluster_claim: Inception-v3 models demonstrate improved performance with multi-crop evaluation, achieving 18.77% Top-1 Error and 4.2% Top-5 Error for a single model, and further enhanced results with ensembles, reaching 17.2-17.3% Top-1 Error and 3.5-3.58% Top-5 Error with multi-crop evaluation.

supported_by_papers.evidence: With an ensemble of 4 models and multi-crop evaluation, we report 3.5% top-5 error and 17.3% top-1 error.

claim_clusters.cluster_claim: The Inception-v3 solution is computationally efficient, requiring significantly less computation and parameters compared to other state-of-the-art denser networks, and its design facilitates training high-quality networks on relatively modest datasets.

supported_by_papers.evidence: Still our solution uses much less computation than the best published results based on denser networks: our model outperforms the results of He et al [6] – cutting the top-5 (top-1) error by 25% (14%) relative, respectively – while being six times cheaper computationally and using at least five times less parameters (estimated).

The combination of lower parameter count and additional regularization with batch-normalized auxiliary classifiers and label-smoothing allows for training high quality networks on relatively modest sized training sets.

unique_claims.claim: General principles and optimization ideas for efficiently scaling up convolutional networks were described.
unique_claims.evidence: In this paper, we start with describing a few general principles and optimization ideas that that proved to be useful for scaling up convolution networks in efficient ways.

unique_claims.claim: High quality results can be achieved with lower-resolution networks, with final result quality quite close to higher resolution counterparts, when computational effort is kept constant.
unique_claims.evidence: Although the lower-resolution networks take longer to train, the quality of the final result is quite close to that of their higher resolution counterparts.
